evidence.detail: The interface defines exactly one operation, void a(rs/x/e), accepting the already-reviewed R29 Stream and no unrelated lifecycle/state method.

All 52 concrete implementations write an outgoing opcode first through Stream.a(int) and then serialize constructor-held packet payload fields with the Stream write-transform methods; examples include opcodes 188, 133, 72, 202 and 210.

Client.a(rs/o/a/a/a) passes the shared output Stream Client.fv to the packet, then forwards the resulting buffer/length to the active connection writer rs/q/b and resets stream bookkeeping. IOException handling disconnects/reconnects the client path.

Concrete implementations are packet-shaped value objects: their constructors capture primitive payload fields (or no payload), and their sole behavior writes one fixed opcode plus those fields into Stream.
This family is distinct from R115 ScriptPacketHandler, which decodes opcode-250 server subprotocol messages; rs/o/a/a/a represents ordinary client-to-server packet serialization.

proposals.note: Corrected from the initially attempted IncomingPacketHandler label after direct inspection of all 52 concrete implementations proved opcode-first serialization into the client output Stream.
